hypothesis: Two-slab K-loop unrolling with paired tl.load A/B and back-to-back tl.dot per iteration will outperform the baseline single-slab K-loop by halving loop trips and overlapping two global to shared movements with two FP32 tl.dot accumulations while using larger-stride a_ptrs += 2*BK and b_ptrs += 2*BK*N pointer advances.
expected_mechanism: Each iteration computes k0 = p*2*BK once, issues tl.load a0/b0 with k0 masks, tl.dot a0*b0 into acc, then tl.load a1 from a_ptrs+BK and b1 from b_ptrs+BK*N with k0+BK masks and second tl.dot a1*b1 into the same FP32 acc, then advances a_ptrs by 2*BK and b_ptrs by 2*BK*N. This halves loop-branch and pointer-update overhead, keeps two BK tiles in flight per loop, gives the pipeliner a larger straight-line load-dot-dot sequence to overlap cp.async movement with mma computation, and leaves a single-slab tail tl.load plus tl.dot for odd tl.cdiv(K,BK). No tile, FP16 I/O, FP32 accumulation, or launcher change.
reasoning_from_feedback: This differs from the prior unevaluated Muse candidate 38b23fad21dc8bb6d194239c7ac0d0a20b1c8566de4055442e3e927d8f97e59a which only hoisted m_mask/n_mask, used one k_off expression, and added tl.range(num_stages=3), and from the human-reviewed trusted implementation 951ec924a4cfa6fb9abd4f9a7d12fbb3e187e56a69b77b8df546cf89b15e63f2 which tested that same mask-hoisting idea. Those sources are distinct; the exact Muse source was not compiled, checked, or timed, so no correctness or speedup claim transfers to this new source. It also keeps baseline program-id mapping and is not grouped_m4 program-id swizzle nor split-K parallelism. The trusted test passed correctness on 512x3072x768, 509x3071x769, 65x129x33 for seeds 42/43 under FP16 torch.mm policy, but that pass applies only to the trusted source. Its median paired screening 1.00239x is ambiguous, not a confirmed gain, especially with A/A median absolute deviation 3.84% and max 10.56% showing screening noise. Compiler evidence showed trusted TTIR only added tt.num_stages=3 while TTGIR kept six async-copies, PTX multisets matched with 18 cp.async, 6 commits, 2 waits, 32 mma.sync, 12 ldmatrix, and resources matched at 120 registers, 0 spills, 24576 bytes shared, which is evidence against a substantive change from mask-hoisting alone. This proposal should survive compilation differently: doubling tl.load/tl.dot per iteration should change TTGIR async-copy count per loop iteration, double cp.async and mma.sync/ldmatrix per iteration in PTX, halve trip count, extend live ranges for a1/b1 and chained acc, and alter shared-memory staging and register pressure, which the compiler cannot fold back to baseline because the two tl.dot operations have an ordered acc dependency with distinct K-mask predicates and distinct pointer offsets.
